q: My sister ___ her guitar every evening.
explain: “My sister” is “she”. In the present simple, he/she/it adds -s: she plays. “Every evening” tells us it is a habit.

q: Tamar ___ eat meat. She’s a vegetarian.
explain: For he/she/it, the negative is doesn’t + verb: Tamar doesn’t eat meat. “Don’t” is for I/you/we/they.

q: “This song is amazing!” “Yes, I ___ with you.”
explain: “Agree” is a verb, so we don’t add “am”: I agree (אני מסכימה). “I am agree” is a translation from Hebrew and is wrong.

q: Look! The dog ___ after the ball.
explain: “Look!” shows that it is happening now, so we use am/is/are + verb-ing: the dog is running.

q: Shira can’t talk on the phone now. She ___ her homework.
explain: Right now, at this moment → present progressive: she is doing her homework. Don’t forget “is”.

q: Ask Yarden, not me. She ___ the answer.
explain: “Know” is a state verb, like like, love, want and need. We don’t use it with -ing, even for now: she knows, not “she is knowing”.

q: Yesterday we ___ to the beach with our friends.
explain: “Go” is an irregular verb: go → went. “Gone” needs have/has: we have gone.

q: We ___ the bus this morning, so we were late for school.
explain: Past simple negative: didn’t + the base verb. “Didn’t caught” is wrong, because “did” already shows the past.

q: “Did you see the game last night?” “Yes, I ___ it on TV.”
explain: See → saw (irregular). “Seen” comes only after have/has/had: I have seen it.

q: There ___ three cats in our garden.
explain: Three cats = more than one → there are. For one thing → there is: there is a cat in the garden.

q: ___ a good café near your school?
explain: To ask a question, put “is” before “there”: Is there…? “A good café” is one place, so not “Are there”.

q: How ___ money do you need for the concert ticket?
explain: We can’t count money (not “two moneys”), so we ask “how much”. “How many” is for things we can count: how many tickets?

q: We didn’t buy ___ bread, so we can’t make sandwiches.
explain: In negative sentences we use “any”: we didn’t buy any bread. “Some” is for positive sentences: we bought some bread.

q: I have ___ good friends in my new class, so I’m not lonely.
explain: We can count friends (one friend, two friends), so we use “a few”. “A little” is for things we can’t count: a little time.

q: You ___ wear a seatbelt in the car. It’s the law.
explain: A rule or a law → must (חייבים). “Mustn’t” means it is not allowed, the opposite.

q: Yael ___ finish her science project by Sunday.
explain: She → has to. After “must” and “can” we never add “to”: she must finish, she can finish.

q: Tomorrow is Saturday, so I ___ get up early. I can sleep late!
explain: “Don’t have to” = it isn’t necessary (לא חייבת). “Mustn’t” = it isn’t allowed (אסור). Getting up early isn’t forbidden, just not necessary.

q: Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
explain: To compare one thing with all the others, we use the superlative: the + adjective + -est. High → the highest.

q: My new phone is ___ than my old one.
explain: Long adjectives use “more”: more expensive. We don’t add -er to them, and we never use “more” and -er together.

q: The new version of the song is much ___ than the old one.
explain: Good → better → best (irregular). “Better” is already a comparative, so “more better” is wrong. “Much better” is correct.

q: “___ do you live?” “In Haifa.”
explain: The answer is a place, so the question word is “where” (איפה).

q: ___ you finish your project yesterday?
explain: “Yesterday” is in the past, so we ask with “did” + the base verb: Did you finish…?

q: Choose the correct question.
options: What time does the film start?
What time does the film starts?
What time is the film start?
explain: Question word + does + subject + base verb. After “does” the verb has no -s: does the film start.

q: My birthday is ___ March.
explain: Months take “in”: in March. Days take “on” (on Monday), and times take “at” (at 5 o’clock).

q: The concert starts ___ 8 o’clock ___ Friday.
explain: Times take “at” (at 8 o’clock), and days take “on” (on Friday).

q: We live ___ the third floor.
explain: In English we live “on” a floor: on the third floor. In Hebrew we say “בקומה”, but “in the third floor” is wrong.

q: The cat is licking ___ paw.
explain: “Its” (no apostrophe) shows belonging: its paw. “It’s” means “it is”: it’s cold today.

q: Adi and I are going to the mall. Do you want to come with ___?
explain: After “with” we use an object pronoun: me, you, him, her, us, them. Adi and I = we → with us.

q: What does “borrow” mean?
explain: Borrow = take something and give it back later: Can I borrow your pen? The opposite is “lend” (להשאיל): I can lend you my pen.

q: What does “tired” mean?
explain: Tired = עייף, when you need to rest or sleep: I’m tired after the long trip.

q: What does “quiet” mean?
explain: Quiet = שקט: The library is quiet. Be careful: “quite” (די) is a different word: The test was quite easy.

q: What does “healthy” mean?
explain: Healthy = בריא: Fruit and vegetables are healthy. The opposite is “unhealthy”.

q: What does “remember” mean?
explain: Remember = לזכור: I remember your phone number. To make someone remember is “remind” (להזכיר): Remind me to call Grandma.

q: What does “invite” mean?
explain: Invite = ask someone to come to an event (להזמין): She invited ten friends to her party.

q: What does “weather” mean?
explain: Weather = מזג אוויר: The weather is sunny today. Don’t mix it up with “whether” (האם), which sounds the same.

q: What is the opposite of “cheap”?
explain: Cheap (זול) ↔ expensive (יקר). “Poor” is the opposite of “rich”.

q: What is the opposite of “early”?
explain: Early (מוקדם) ↔ late (מאוחר): I got up early, but my brother got up late.

q: What is the opposite of “win”?
explain: Win (לנצח) ↔ lose (להפסיד). Watch the spelling: “loose”, with two o’s, means not tight (רפוי).

q: I’m ___. Can I have a sandwich?
explain: Hungry = רעב, you want to eat. Thirsty = צמא, you want to drink.

q: Can you ___ the music down? I’m trying to study.
explain: Turn down = make the sound quieter (להנמיך). Turn up = make it louder.

q: We ___ a lot of photos on our trip to Eilat.
explain: In English we “take” photos (לצלם): She took a photo of the sunset. We don’t say “make photos”.

q: Romi is very good ___ drawing. Her pictures are amazing.
explain: We say “good at” something: good at drawing, good at chess. Not “good in”, which is a translation of “טובה ב…”.

q: Which word means “a place where you can borrow books”?
explain: In a library (ספרייה) you borrow books and give them back. In a bookshop (חנות ספרים) you buy them.

q: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
explain: A guitar, a piano and drums are musical instruments. A kitchen is a room in a house.

q: Ella is very ___. She always helps other people.
explain: Kind = nice and good to others (טובת לב). Lazy, rude and selfish people don’t usually help others.

q: Don’t ___ to bring your swimsuit tomorrow!
explain: “Don’t forget to…” (אל תשכחי) means “remember to…”. “Don’t remember to bring” says the opposite and doesn’t make sense.

q: I always ___ my homework before dinner.
explain: We “do” homework, not “make” it. Other phrases with “do”: do the dishes, do an exercise.

q: Hila says: “I can’t stand loud music.” What does she mean?
options: She really doesn’t like loud music.
She can’t stand up when the music is loud.
explain: “I can’t stand…” means “I hate…” (אני לא סובלת). It has nothing to do with standing up.

q: It’s ___ cold today. Take a coat.
explain: Before an adjective like “cold” we use “really” or “very”. “Very much” and “a lot” go with verbs: I like it very much.

q: The film was so ___ that I fell asleep in the middle.
explain: -ing describes the thing: the film was boring (משעמם). -ed describes how a person feels: I was bored (השתעממתי).

q: Can I ___ at your drawing?
explain: We “look at” something (להסתכל על). “See” and “watch” don’t take “at”: Can I see your drawing?

q: It’s dark in here. Can you ___ the light, please?
explain: In English we “turn on” (or “switch on”) a light, a phone or the TV. “Open the light” is a translation from Hebrew.

q: Which word has the same meaning as “huge”?
explain: Huge = enormous = very, very big (ענק). “Tiny” is the opposite: very small.

q: Read: “Tal has a dog called Pepper. Every morning before school, she takes Pepper for a walk in the park.” When does Tal walk her dog?
explain: The text says: “Every morning before school”.

q: Read: “My name is Michal. I have two brothers: Ido is fifteen and Ben is eight. I’m twelve.” Which sentence is true?
explain: Ido is 15, Michal is 12 and Ben is 8. So Ido is older (מבוגר יותר) than Michal, and Michal is older than Ben.

q: Read: “Omer wanted to buy new headphones, but they cost 300 shekels. He only had 180, so he decided to save his pocket money for two more months.” Why didn’t Omer buy the headphones?
explain: The headphones cost 300 shekels and Omer only had 180. He needs to save more money first.

q: Read: “Yuval opened the window and smiled. The sun was shining, and her friends were already waiting downstairs with their bikes.” What will Yuval probably do next?
options: Go for a bike ride with her friends
Stay at home and watch TV
explain: Her friends are waiting with bikes and the weather is nice, so she will probably join them. “Probably” (כנראה) means we guess from clues in the text.

q: Read: “For a whole month before the school concert, Maya played the piano for two hours every day. At the concert, she didn’t make a single mistake.” Why did Maya play so well?
options: She worked hard before the concert.
explain: She played for two hours every day for a month. Her hard work helped her play without mistakes. The text says nothing about the other answers.

q: Read: “Lior’s phone fell into the pool at a party. When she took it out, the screen was black and it didn’t turn on.” How did Lior probably feel?
explain: Her phone stopped working, so she probably felt upset (מוטרדת, עצובה).

q: Read: “Penguins are birds, but they can’t fly. They use their wings to swim very fast under water.” What do penguins use their wings for?
explain: The text says: “They use their wings to swim”. Penguins can’t fly.

q: Read: “Shani’s family moved from Tel Aviv to a small village in the north. She misses her old friends, but she loves the quiet streets and the green hills.” Which sentence is true?
options: Shani likes some things about her new home.
Shani doesn’t miss her old friends.
Shani still lives in Tel Aviv.
explain: She misses her friends, but she loves the quiet streets and the hills. So she likes some things about the village.

q: Read: “The school trip is on Thursday. Bring water, a hat and a packed lunch. Phones are allowed, but music speakers are not.” What can’t students bring on the trip?
explain: “Music speakers are not allowed” means you can’t bring them (אסור).

q: Read: “Gili’s grandmother is eighty, but she swims every morning and goes to a dance class twice a week. ‘Age is just a number,’ she likes to say.” What does she mean?
options: You can be active at any age.
She doesn’t know how old she is.
explain: She is eighty but very active. She means that your age doesn’t decide what you can do.

q: Read: “Amit forgot his sister’s birthday. In the evening, he came home with flowers and a long letter that began with ‘I’m so sorry’.” Why did Amit bring flowers?
options: To say sorry for forgetting her birthday
Because his sister asked for flowers
To thank his sister for a present
explain: He forgot the birthday, and his letter begins with “I’m so sorry”. The flowers are part of his apology (התנצלות).

q: Read: “This is the best café in town! The cakes are amazing and the music is great. The only problem: it’s always full, so come early.” What is the problem with the café?
explain: The writer says “it’s always full”. Full of people = crowded (צפוף).

q: Read: “Roni and Inbar planned to see a film together on Saturday night. On Saturday afternoon, Inbar called: she had a high fever and had to stay in bed.” What probably happened on Saturday night?
options: The girls didn’t see the film together.
Inbar went to the film alone.
explain: Inbar was sick in bed, so the two girls couldn’t go to the film together.

q: Read: “When Hadas got to the bus stop, she saw the number 5 bus driving away. She looked at her watch and sighed: the next one was in forty minutes.” What happened?
options: She got on the number 5 bus.
explain: The bus was driving away when she arrived, so she missed it (פספסה) and had to wait for the next one.

q: Read: “In her first week at the new school, Eden spent every break alone in the library. In the second week, a girl from her class asked her to join a basketball game. By the end of the month, Eden had lots of friends.” What is the text mostly about?
options: Eden making friends at a new school
explain: The text shows how Eden goes from being alone to having many friends. That is the main idea (הרעיון המרכזי).

q: Read: “Hi Nitzan! I can’t come to dance practice today because I have a dentist appointment. Can you tell the teacher? Thanks! Rachel” Why did Rachel write this message?
options: To ask Nitzan to pass on a message
To invite Nitzan to the dentist
To ask when dance practice starts
To say that she has a new teacher
explain: Rachel asks Nitzan to tell the teacher that she can’t come. That is the purpose (המטרה) of the message.

q: Read: “Every summer, sea turtles come to Israel’s beaches to lay their eggs in the sand. Volunteers protect the eggs so that dogs and people don’t hurt them.” Why do volunteers protect the eggs?
options: To keep them safe from dogs and people
To move them to the zoo
explain: The text says the volunteers protect the eggs “so that dogs and people don’t hurt them”.

q: What does “typical” mean?
explain: A typical day is a normal, usual day.

q: What does “activity” mean?
explain: Swimming and drawing are activities: things you do.

q: What does “bridge” mean?
explain: You cross a river on a bridge.

q: What does “choice” mean?
explain: You can choose: you have a choice.

q: What does “danger” mean?
explain: “Danger” is a noun (סכנה). “Dangerous” is the adjective (מסוכן).

q: What does “journey” mean?
explain: A long trip from one place to another.

q: What does “mountain” mean?
explain: Mount Hermon is the highest mountain in Israel.

q: What does “village” mean?
explain: A village is a small place to live, smaller than a town.

q: What does “river” mean?
explain: The Jordan is a river.

q: What does “wide” mean?
explain: The opposite of “wide” is “narrow”.

q: What does “depend on” mean?
explain: You can depend on a good friend.

q: What does “realize” mean?
explain: “I suddenly realized I forgot my keys.”

q: What does “prefer” mean?
explain: “I prefer tea to coffee.”

q: What does “fix” mean?
explain: “Dad can fix my bike.”

q: What does “continue” mean?
explain: “Please continue reading.”

q: What does “imagine” mean?
explain: “Imagine you can fly!”

q: What does “unusual” mean?
explain: “Un-” means “not”: unusual = not usual.

q: What does “possible” mean?
explain: The opposite is “impossible”.

q: Be ___! The road is wet.
explain: “Be careful” means תיזהר / תיזהרי.

q: Swimming in the sea at night is ___.
explain: After “is” we need an adjective: dangerous. “Danger” is a noun.

q: We crossed the river on a long ___.
explain: You cross a river on a bridge.

q: I can’t ___ my phone. Can you help me?
explain: To fix = to repair, make it work again.

q: Snow in Tel Aviv is very ___.
explain: It almost never snows in Tel Aviv, so it is unusual.

q: Which word is the opposite of “narrow”?
explain: Narrow = צר; wide = רחב.

q: What does “advice” mean?
explain: “My mom gave me good advice.”

q: What does “agree” mean?
explain: “I agree with you” = I think the same.

q: What does “allow” mean?
explain: “My parents allow me to stay up late on Fridays.”

q: What does “arrive” mean?
explain: “The bus arrives at eight.”

q: What does “brave” mean?
explain: A brave person does something even when it is scary.

q: What does “celebrate” mean?
explain: “We celebrate birthdays with a cake.”

q: What does “choose” mean?
explain: “Choose” is the verb; “choice” is the noun.

q: What does “collect” mean?
explain: “She collects stickers.”

q: What does “decide” mean?
explain: “I can’t decide which dress to buy.”

q: What does “discover” mean?
explain: “Scientists discovered a new planet.”

q: What does “explain” mean?
explain: “Can you explain the homework to me?”

q: What does “famous” mean?
explain: Everybody knows a famous person.

q: What does “guess” mean?
explain: “I don’t know the answer, so I’ll guess.”

q: What does “improve” mean?
explain: “Practice every day and your English will improve.”

q: What does “mistake” mean?
explain: “Everyone makes mistakes.”

q: What does “neighbor” mean?
explain: A neighbor lives next to you.

q: What does “promise” mean?
explain: “I promise I’ll be home by ten.”

q: What does “proud” mean?
explain: “My parents were proud of my grades.”

q: What does “share” mean?
explain: “Let’s share the pizza.”

q: What does “worry” mean?
explain: “Don’t worry, everything will be OK.”

q: I can’t ___ which ice cream to buy. They all look good!
explain: To decide = להחליט.

q: Can you ___ this word to me? I don’t understand it.
explain: To explain = להסביר.

q: The train will ___ at 5 o’clock.
explain: To arrive = להגיע.

q: It’s OK to make ___. That’s how we learn.
explain: Mistakes = טעויות.

q: She was ___ enough to jump into the cold water and save the dog.
explain: Brave = אמיץ: doing something scary.

q: My little brother and I ___ a room.
explain: To share a room = לחלוק חדר.

q: My teacher gave me some good ___ about how to study for the test.
explain: Advice (עצה) has no plural: some advice, good advice.

q: Which word is the opposite of “agree”?
explain: Dis- + agree = not agree.

q: Which word is the opposite of “arrive”?
explain: Arrive = to come to a place; leave = to go away from it.

q: We ___ my grandmother’s 80th birthday with the whole family.
explain: To celebrate = לחגוג (past: celebrated).

q: Read: “Noa gets up at 6:30 every morning. She eats breakfast, takes the bus to school and starts her first lesson at eight.” What time does Noa get up?
explain: The first sentence says she gets up at 6:30.

q: Read: “The village is small and quiet. There is one shop, one school and a wide river with an old bridge.” What is there in the village?
explain: “A wide river with an old bridge.”

q: Read: “Tom wanted to climb the mountain, but it started to rain. ‘It’s dangerous,’ said his dad. ‘We’ll try again tomorrow.’” Why didn’t they climb the mountain?
options: Because it was raining and dangerous
explain: Rain made the path dangerous, so Dad said they would try again tomorrow.

q: Read: “Maya prefers reading to watching TV. Every weekend she goes to the library and borrows three books.” What can we learn about Maya?
explain: She prefers reading and borrows books every weekend: she loves reading.
